_comment: Token pricing for the cost meter (src/cost/cli.ts, `npm run cost-meter`).
`multipliers` are structural — they follow from how prompt caching is billed,
not from any one model's price sheet — so they rarely need touching.
`inputPerMTok` is USD per million INPUT tokens and starts null on purpose:
a stale hardcoded price silently corrupts every dollar figure, while a
missing one makes the report fall back to input-equivalent units, which are
exact. Filled in 2026-08-03 from Anthropic's published API pricing.
The multipliers above were checked against that same source and match it
exactly: output is 5x input on every model listed, cache read is 0.1x, and
cache write is 1.25x (5m TTL) / 2.0x (1h TTL). No per-model override needed.
DATED: claude-sonnet-5 is at introductory pricing of $2.00/MTok through
2026-08-31 and reverts to $3.00 on 2026-09-01. The value below is the
introductory one — after that date it reads ~33% low until changed.
A key of the form `model@speed` prices Claude Code's fast mode, which bills
Opus at twice the standard rate while reporting the same model string. Any
speed with no entry here is UNPRICED, not standard-priced: the session's usd
comes back null rather than half the real figure. Fast mode exists on
claude-opus-5 and claude-opus-4-8 only — it was removed from opus-4-7.
`charsPerToken` is used ONLY to turn suppressed byte counts into an estimated
token count. Nothing in the absolute accounting depends on it.
